summary: POC scoping for benchmark planning and harness integration. Discussed workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, metrics to collect (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens), sample harness scripts, and security prerequisites for a Private/VPC run. Agreed to share harness template and run an end-to-end benchmark the week of 2026-12-14.
topics: benchmark harness integration and example scripts
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE. with me is Asha our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Marcus: Marcus here, Head of ML at Sentinel. Priya and Daniel are on too.
[00:12] Priya: hey, thanks.
[00:14] Daniel: hi. audio's a bit low on my side.
[00:18] Asha: can you hear ok now Daniel?
[00:20] Daniel: yep better, thanks.
[00:24] Samir: Cool. Goal for today: scope the POC benchmarks and how your harness will plug into Redwood. We want to capture success criteria, the workload sizing, and confirm streaming vs non-streaming expectations.
[00:36] Marcus: Great. High level — we want to validate latency and cost targets for our generation workloads. Specifically p95 end-to-end under 350ms for non-streaming short responses (~150 tokens) and decent throughput for batch jobs. Also quality must not regress more than 3% on our eval metrics when using quantized models.
[00:52] Asha: good, that gives us concrete numbers. Two quick clarifications: when you say end-to-end p95, is that client-to-client including your app processing and network? or strictly inference server side?
[01:02] Marcus: good call. We want both. Server-side p95 target is 200ms, end-to-end probably 350ms after accounting for network and our app.
[01:09] Asha: understood. For the POC we'll run server-side benchmarks first then one end-to-end run including your edge.
[01:15] Priya: On workload sizing — our production sees spikes up to ~1,200 rps for short-generation endpoints, sustained ~300 rps, average payload 120 tokens. For embeddings we have separate batch windows at night retrieving ~150k items.
[01:28] Asha: ok that's helpful. For the harness we'll need a representative sample of prompts and a 24h traffic histogram, that lets us synthesize realistic concurrency.
[01:36] Samir: we'll provide a harness template — it's basically a small runner that can call the Redwood API in streaming or non-streaming mode, capture timing per phase (TTFB, first-token, last-token, post-processing), and emit Prometheus-style metrics.
[01:48] Marcus: what's the tech for the harness? do you prefer k6 / locust / custom python script?
[01:52] Asha: we support multiple. For streaming tests we usually recommend a small Node harness we provide because k6 doesn't do streaming well; locust is fine for non-streaming. We'll attach sample scripts.
[02:03] Priya: can you share the Node streaming example? streaming is one of our bigger unknowns — we want to measure first-token latency and ordering with our client streaming pipeline.
[02:12] Asha: yes, we'll share node-streaming.js. FYI transcript may say "streaming" as "streamingg" sometimes — apologies, auto-transcribe..
[02:20] Daniel: security question — we probably will need to run Private/VPC for the final runs. What do you need from us?
[02:25] Samir: typical stuff: IP allowlists, KMS key ARNs if you want customer-managed keys, SAML SSO for console, and SOC2 attestation. We'll send our security pack but Daniel, anything special for Sentinel?
[02:36] Daniel: we need audit log retention to 1 year and ability to rotate keys via our HSM. Also ensure for the POC the data doesn't leave our VPC.
[02:44] Asha: that's doable — for the POC we can spin up a Private control plane in your VPC or do a VPC peering flow; both options have slightly different timelines.
[02:53] Marcus: timeline question — how long to get Private POC infra up?
[02:56] Samir: if we go VPC peering and you already have infra and SRE capacity, ~2 weeks to provision and baseline test. If you want an on-prem air-gapped package it's longer. For hosted + dedicated tests (no VPC) we can run initial benchmarks in 2-3 days.
[03:09] Priya: ok for scope let's plan hosted first, then Private for the final gated run.
[03:13] Samir: perfect. On metrics — we'll collect p50/p95/p99 for first-token and last-token, tokens/sec, cpu/gpu utilization, memory, batch sizes, and cost per 1k tokens. Also we'll track quality via your eval harness (we can run your prompts and compute pass/fail rates).
[03:29] Marcus: re quality, we'll supply a 1k prompt subset we label as critical — success criteria is >=97% pass on that set vs baseline model.
[03:36] Asha: noted. Also pro tip: quantization can change outputs slightly. We'll recommend 4-bit quant or int8 profiles and show diff metrics. If mismatch is over 3% we can try alternate model variants or fallback routing.
[03:48] Priya: about workload sizing — you mentioned batching; what's typical batch sizes Redwood uses for small-gen models?
[03:53] Asha: it depends on model and seq length. For 120 token avg payloads, we typically see beneficial batching at concurrency >16 with batch sizes up to 64 depending on queuing latency tolerance. We'll give recommended autoscale thresholds.
[04:05] Lena: any guidance on GPU types? we currently run on A100 in prod but open to cheaper GPUs if performance-cost tradeoff is good.
[04:12] Asha: A100 is great for large context; for quantized workloads Ampere T4-like or L4 can be cost effective. We'll recommend a matrix (latency vs cost per 1k tokens) in the writeup.
[04:22] Marcus: ok. I want to dig into streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs — our UX needs first token fast (so streaming appeals), but we worry about throughput for bursty traffic.
[04:33] Samir: streaming reduces perceived latency because you get tokens earlier; server-side cost is similar overall but streaming can limit batching efficiency since you need to flush earlier. In practice we measure ~20-40% worse throughput for strictly streaming-first-token-optimized runs vs batch optimized non-streaming. But for many UX-sensitive endpoints it's worth it.
[04:52] Priya: can the harness emulate hybrid mode — start streaming and then allow coalescing for later tokens?
[04:57] Asha: yes, we have a "hybrid" pattern in the sample harness where initial token is streamed and subsequent tokens are buffered slightly to allow small batching windows. We'll include that.
[05:07] Marcus: for the benchmark schedule, propose steps?
[05:10] Samir: Step 1: exchange prompt set and traffic histogram. Step 2: Redwood shares harness template + node/python examples for streaming and non-streaming. Step 3: we run server-side benchmarks on hosted for server perf (2-3 days). Step 4: run end-to-end with your app in staging incl VPC peering if needed. Step 5: review results and iterate.
[05:28] Priya: timeline sounds good. aim for server-side run week of 12/14 and end-to-end week of 12/21?
[05:33] Samir: yes that seems workable. We'll block time.
[05:37] Daniel: regarding logs and IOCs, can we get request-level logs masked for PII?
[05:41] Asha: yes we can obfuscate PII fields and provide token-level cost breakdowns but raw logs can be restricted to your VPC in Private mode.
[05:49] Marcus: are there any known gotchas with the harness?
[05:52] Asha: a few: clock skew on clients can mess with timing measurements, not flushing streaming buffers artificially low concurrency can create odd queuing effects, and client retries can inflate apparent throughput — we'll include a test checklist.
[06:05] Samir: we'll also provide a small benchmark spreadsheet so you can compare runs across model variants, quantization profiles, and hardware.
[06:12] Priya: perfect. One more — cost estimates. Can you give rough numbers for expected cost per 1M tokens on hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[06:20] Samir: rough back-of-envelope: hosted varies by model size but assume $X-$Y per 1M tokens; dedicated reduces unit cost by ~30-50% with committed usage. We'll send a clearer cost matrix in the followup.
[06:33] Marcus: ok. anything else on acceptance?
[06:36] Priya: we want documented repro steps for each benchmark and a runbook to reproduce the runs in case of flaky results.
[06:42] Asha: we'll include runbooks + CI-friendly commands so you can plug into your existing perf CI.
[06:47] Samir: quick recap and next steps — Samir to share harness and sample scripts; Asha to recommend configs; Priya to share prompts and histogram; Daniel to confirm security items. We'll target server-side run week of 12/14.
[06:59] Marcus: thanks all. schedule follow-up for 12/13 to review harness?
[07:03] Samir: yes I'll put a calendar invite. thanks everyone.
[07:07] (call ends)
